title: Prepare a reusable Zedu booth and QR handoff kit for in-person education events
description: Design materials for a team member introducing Zedu at an in-person education conference or bootcamp fair. Distinct from co-hosted online events and webinar planning. Deliver a 30-second explanation, printable one-page handout, verified-claim demo cue card, accessible short URL plus tested QR destination, and an optional lead-consent/handoff process with a named responder. Compare three event contexts and recommend when attending is worthwhile using sourced audience fit and disclosed cost unknowns. Done when the team approves the kit, printed-size QR tests are documented, all claims trace to current evidence and follow-up permissions are clear. No event booking, printing spend, lead collection, outreach or publication without approval.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add a consent-based lead card and a 48-hour follow-up sequence, so booth conversations turn into sign-ups
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A booth produces conversations that are forgotten by the next week. Approach: a short lead card or form (name, role, institution, what they want to try, an explicit consent tick for follow-up under Nigeria's Data Protection Act), a rule for where the cards are stored and when they are deleted, and a two-message follow-up sent within 48 hours with a direct link to set up a workspace. Done: the card design, the consent wording, the storage rule and the follow-up messages.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the booth kit on the two store links that work today, and keep the /download QR out of it until it's fixed
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Checked 22 Oct 2026: the App Store (id6759181591) and Google Play (net.emerj.zedu) listings are live, but the 'scan to download' block on zedu.chat/download is an empty placeholder and the desktop button links nowhere, so a booth kit must not send people there yet. Plan: 1) generate printable QR codes that go straight to each store listing, decode-check each one, and test them on an iPhone and an Android phone from a printed copy at booth distance; 2) write a one-page handout and a table sign that say only what's on the live product pages, with no unsourced numbers (the homepage store ratings don't match the stores today); 3) a short booth script and a sign-up tracking sheet with UTM-tagged links per event. Tasks: QR codes and print test (other), handout, sign and script (content).
